scenes.text: Some AI models you can only use through a website or an API. [1] Others, you can download for free, and run on your own computer. [2] What's the difference, and which should you pick? Let's talk open versus closed models.

title: Open vs
Closed
data.subtitle: Which AI model should you use?

scenes.text: Here's the core difference. [1] A closed model stays on the company's servers. You send a request, and get an answer back. GPT, Claude, and Gemini work like this. [2] An open weights model can be downloaded, and run anywhere. Llama, Qwen, Mistral, and DeepSeek are examples.

[1] So what does open weights mean? [2] Remember, the weights are the billions of numbers the model learned. [3] Open weights means those numbers are shared publicly. [4] But the training data and code are often still private, so it's not always fully open source.

data.definition: A model whose learned numbers, the weights, are published so anyone can download and run it.

scenes.text: Each side has strengths. [1] Closed models are often the most capable, easy to start with, and need no hardware. [2] Open models give you privacy, control, no per-request fees, and you can fine-tune them freely.

[1] Here's a quick guide. [2] Building a quick prototype? Start with a closed API. [3] Handling private hospital or bank data? Open models on your own servers. [4] Need the very best reasoning? Often closed. [5] Running offline on a phone? A small open model.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think open models are always free. [2] The download is free, but running them isn't. You pay for GPUs, electricity, and engineers. At small scale, an API can even be cheaper.

data.fact: The download is free, but GPUs, electricity and engineers cost money. At small scale, an API can be cheaper.
data.tip: Free to download, not free to run

scenes.text: In practice, many companies mix both. [1] A closed model for hard reasoning tasks, [2] a small open model for simple, high volume jobs, [3] and open models on their own servers for sensitive data.

Quick quiz! A hospital wants patient data to never leave its own servers. Which is the better fit? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] An open model running on their own servers, so the data never leaves!

data.question: Data must stay in-house. Which fits?

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] Closed models are used through an API. [2] Open weights models can be downloaded and run anywhere. [3] Closed is easy and powerful, while open gives privacy and control. [4] And open is free to download, not free to run. [5] Next, small language models. Follow AI Maastaaru!
